newsitem.title: USA: Vote set for Milwaukee baseball stadium bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Vote set for Milwaukee baseball stadium bond issue.

text.p: A vote on a resolution allowing the issuance of $160 million of tax-exempt bonds for a new stadium for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team has been scheduled for Friday afternoon.

The agenda for the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District board meeting includes a resolution for the bond issue as well as reports from the senior banker, financial adviser and bond counsel for the controversial debt issue.
If the resolution is approved, plans call for selling the bonds sometime next month, according to Pat Born, a senior vice president at Evenson Dodge Inc., the financial adviser.
Born said meetings with rating agencies and bond insurers have been scheduled for next week.
"Our expectation is that the underlying credit is an investment grade credit," he added.

However, a five-county sales tax slated to repay the bonds is still being contested in court. While a lawsuit, brought by a group of Milwaukee area taxpayers, has been dismissed by the Wisconsin Supreme Court and by a U.S. District Court judge in Milwaukee, the group has filed an appeal of the federal court's dismissal with the U.S. Appellate Court in Chicago.

Douglass Bartley, an attorney representing the taxpayers, said the case is currently in the briefing stage. The group contended that the 0.1 percent sales tax imposed by the state legislature is unconstitutional.
Analysts at Fitch Investors Service, Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp. said this week they would examine the lawsuit as part of their review of the credit.

Jon Axelrod, an attorney representing state officials in the lawsuit, has said that he would forward an opinion to bond counsel on the $160 million bond issue that the lawsuit has no merit. Last month, the baseball district board threatened monetary sanctions against the taxpayer litigants if they persist with the lawsuit.

In addition to proceeds from the bond issue, the $250 million convertible-roofed stadium would be funded with $50 million in loans to the Brewers from the city of Milwaukee, the local business community and two foundations, and $40 million from the sale of naming rights to Miller Brewing Co., upfront concession payments and a $10 million letter of credit from the American Baseball League.
